messages:
sophie (product): OrbitPay just opened a high-priority support case — p95 on chat endpoints jumped ~3x after the v1.3 rollout. Copying the support logs below. Need product decision: backlog investigation vs immediate rollback. @raj @daniel please triage. Ticket SUP-4821

maya (support): adding context — spike started ~2025-11-02T02:14Z immediately after deploy-bot: rollout v1.3 -> model: llama-70b-quant. Metrics: p50 ~120ms -> 160ms, p95 ~180ms -> 540ms. Customer on Dedicated, steady qps ~200, typical prompt length ~900 tokens. Customer unhappy, asking for mitigation.

deploy-bot: rollout v1.3 (model/llama-70b-quant) completed at 2025-11-02T02:10:18Z :package:

daniel (eng-runtime): I'll start by pulling traces and kernel selection logs. Can you paste a representative request payload and the model config (seq len, batching, kv-cache settings)?

sophie (product): Sample from OrbitPay (redacted): prompt_tokens=900, convo_history enabled, batching disabled (customer choice). They rely heavily on prefix/KV caching for repeated short follow-ups. Acceptance criteria proposal for a backlog item: reproduce end-to-end, root cause analysis, regression alerting added, automated fallback routing to compatible variant, updated runbook + customer comms.

raj (eng-platform): Early options for immediate mitigation:
- Rollback model to v1.2 for OrbitPay tenant only (fast, known safe)
- Route OrbitPay to a smaller quantized variant (llama-70b-q4f) as a temporary policy
- Force different kernel selection or sequence-chop at the routing layer
Rollback downside: loses perf gains other customers may have. Routing tweak is lowest blast radius.

lena (sales): OrbitPay is an enterprise customer (contracted SLA). They want ETA within 24h and may apply credit if we don't commit to a mitigation. We need a clear customer-facing plan ASAP.

maya (support): temporary routing snippet that we can apply via console (customer-scoped policy):
```
{"tenant_id": "orbitpay-01", "route": {"model": "llama-70b-v1.2", "policy": "force"}}
```
This will route all requests from that tenant to v1.2 until we flip it back.

deploy-bot: note — Canary rollout for v1.3 targeted a 5% slice earlier; finalization occurred at 02:10.

daniel (eng-runtime): Quick debug update: traces show attention kernel fallback for sequences >512; fused KV caching paths weren't hit due to changed op ordering in v1.3 optimizer. That increases per-token work and ups p95 for long prompts. I have a repro script that simulates 900-token requests and reproduces ~3x p95 locally.

raj (eng-platform): I can push a tenant-level routing override for OrbitPay in ~30m if product signs off. We'll also add a temporary metric alert for p95 > 300ms on that tenant.

sophie (product): Decision (proposal):
1) Immediate mitigation: apply tenant routing override to v1.2 for OrbitPay (raj) — timeline: within 1 hour.
2) Backlog item: PROD-6523 — "Investigate v1.3 latency regression for long-sequence/dedicated workloads" (owner: daniel)
3) Launch criteria for the PROD-6523 backlog: reproduce, root cause, regression test added to CI, automated fallback policy implemented, runbook + customer comms drafted.
4) Priority: P1 (enterprise SLA breach risk). ETA: mitigation live in 1 hour; full RCA + fixes aimed for 48 hours.

lena (sales): I'll notify OrbitPay with the 48h plan and interim routing change. They requested a standby sync — I'll offer a 30min bridge after mitigation is live.

maya (support): On it — I'll patch SUP-4821 with the routing workaround and add the repro snippet we used. Will also request screenshots/latency graphs from the customer to confirm improvement.

raj (eng-platform): Rolling override now for tenant=orbitpay-01 -> model=llama-70b-v1.2. Applying rule in 2...1... applied. New rule id: route-override-8274.

deploy-bot: applied route override route-override-8274 at 2025-11-02T02:39:12Z :white_check_mark:

daniel (eng-runtime): After routing change, we saw p95 drop back to ~190ms in our staging replay of OrbitPay traffic. We'll continue root cause work and aim to have a regression test for seq>512 in the next PR.

sophie (product): Thanks all. I'll open PROD-6523 and add the acceptance criteria we discussed. Assigning: daniel (owner), raj (mitigation/ops), maya (customer comms), product will review runbook before close.

lena (sales): Thanks — I'll update the customer and schedule the bridge.

maya (support): :thumbsup: SUP-4821 updated with mitigation steps and ETA.
